ALBANIA is on the Adriatic Sea opposite the heel of Italy. On the north and east is Yugo-Slavia and on the south and east is Greece.

Roughly the population is about 1,000,000. The area is 30,800 square kilometers. It has a democratic form of government, with four Regents acting in the executive capacity, a Prime Minister and Cabinet and a legislative body whose members are indirectly elected through universal male suffrage. This body has the real power of governing. It is called the Parliament or Chamber of Deputies. The members of the Cabinet represent the following departments:
Foreign Affairs, Interior, Finance, Public Works and Education.

Probably the root stock of the Albanians is the ancient Pelasgians, later Albania was called Illyria. Successive contests and occupations followed by the Romans, Greeks, Slavs and Turk. Many Roman ruins are still evident in the country, especially at Durazzo which was the starting point of the road to Byzance and for a time was the home of Cicero du-ring his exile. In 1912 an independent government was set up which ended the Turkish domination. During the war the Serbs, Austrians and Italians successively occupied the country.
The fall the great European Powers have formally recognized Albania and it has become a member of the League of Nations. An Albanian Red Cross is beeing organized at this time.
In religion the people are largely Mohammedan but in the north there is a good sized Roman Catholic element and in the south the Greek Orthodox faith is strong.

The men dress in native costumes. They are dark skinned and have eyes of blue or brown. They are fearful and good warriors but are peaceful and prefer peace and agriculture to war. They use primitive farm tools and they donkey is the most popular means of locomotion. They show deep respect for their women and in spite of their Mohammedism it is seldom a man hay plural wives.

The men are cool and self poised. Honesty is a chief virtue and once an Albanian gives his word he would prefer death to breaking his bond. Given a period of freedom from the attacks of their neighbors there is little doubt of their $ showing remarkable advances along all lines.
